word_order: SVO — sample sentences place subjects before verbs and objects (e.g. “皮特曼 认为 天气情况 要到下周 才能 改善”, “夏季 漫长的 白昼 会 导致 睡眠不足”)
punctuation_present: always — the samples consistently use Chinese punctuation (commas, periods, quotes, parentheses, etc.)
register: formal written informative prose (encyclopedic / guide / news-like sentences)
non_boundary_traps: 年 (dates like “1767 年”) — numeric+unit groups
序列或列表 separated by “、” (enumeration comma)
notes_for_prompt_writer: Chinese text has no spaces; segmentation must rely on characters, punctuation and clause structure. Prefer splitting at strong sentence-final punctuation (。！？；) and at coordinating/subordinating conjunction boundaries, but treat commas (，) with caution since they often occur inside noun phrases, relative clauses, or enumerations (、). Never begin a segment with trailing punctuation characters listed above; avoid splitting immediately after prepositions/conjunctions in unstable_prefix_signals because the clause is likely incomplete.
